original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-descending-types-morphisms}
Let $\mathcal{P}$ be a property of morphisms of schemes over a base.
Let $\tau \in \{fpqc, fppf, \etale, smooth, syntomic\}$.
Suppose that
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\mathcal{P}$ is stable under any base change
(see Schemes, Definition \ref{schemes-definition-preserved-by-base-change}),
\item if $Y_j \to V_j$, $j = 1, \ldots, m$ have $\mathcal{P}$,
then so does $\coprod Y_j \to \coprod V_j$, and
\item for any surjective morphism of affines
$X \to S$ which is flat, flat of finite presentation,
\'etale, smooth or syntomic depending on whether $\tau$ is
fpqc, fppf, \'etale, smooth, or syntomic,
any descent datum $(V, \varphi)$ relative
to $X$ over $S$ such that $\mathcal{P}$ holds for
$V \to X$ is effective.
\end{enumerate}
Then morphisms of type $\mathcal{P}$ satisfy descent for $\tau$-coverings.

hypotheses: P is a property of morphisms over a base.
P is preserved under ARBITRARY base changes.
P is preserved under FINITE disjoint unions of morphisms.
For any surjective affine τ-associated map X→S (flat; flat finitely presented; étale; smooth; syntomic), every descent datum (V,φ) over X/S for which V→X has P is effective.
conclusions: Morphisms with property P satisfy descent for τ-covering families.
semantic_review_note: Three independent hypotheses: stability under any base change, finite coproduct preservation, and effectiveness for local affine τ-covers. Do not infer effective descent for arbitrary schemes absent conditions.

original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-affine}
Let $S$ be a scheme.
Let $\{X_i \to S\}_{i\in I}$ be an fpqc covering, see
Topologies, Definition \ref{topologies-definition-fpqc-covering}.
Let $(V_i/X_i, \varphi_{ij})$ be a descent datum
relative to $\{X_i \to S\}$. If each morphism
$V_i \to X_i$ is affine, then the descent datum is
effective.
statement:
Let $S$ be a scheme.
Let $\{X_i \to S\}_{i\in I}$ be an fpqc covering, see
Topologies, Definition \ref{topologies-definition-fpqc-covering}.
Let $(V_i/X_i, \varphi_{ij})$ be a descent datum
relative to $\{X_i \to S\}$. If each morphism
$V_i \to X_i$ is affine, then the descent datum is
effective.
hypotheses: (V_i→X_i,φ_ij) is a scheme descent datum for that covering.
conclusions: The descent datum is EFFECTIVE, i.e., arises (up to isomorphism) from an S-scheme with the canonical descent datum.
semantic_review_note: Fpqc effectivity for affine descent data. This is an existence of descended S-scheme, not an assertion that every scheme descent datum is effective.

hypotheses: S is an object of Sch_τ.
conclusions: There is an equivalence between (i) compatible scheme descent data (X_i,φ_ii') with X_i objects of the chosen big τ-site and (ii) sheaves F on (Sch/S)_τ such that h_(S_i)×F is representable for EVERY i.
Under the equivalence, the representing objects for h_(S_i)×F correspond to the X_i.
Such a sheaf F is representable iff the corresponding descent datum is effective.
semantic_review_note: Representability criterion is a biconditional, nested within a category equivalence. The original source footnote explicitly excludes fpqc, and one must keep every X_i in site objects.
